title: OSHA general industry permit-required confined spaces practice questions
description: Free OSHA general industry permit-required confined spaces practice questions on 29 CFR 1910.146. Every answer is explained and linked to the rule.

questions.question: Under 1910.146(a), which type of employment is outside the scope of the permit-required confined spaces section?

options.A: Warehouse employment
options.B: Construction
options.C: Food processing employment
options.D: Chemical plant employment

questions.explanation: The section "does not apply to agriculture, to construction, or to shipyard employment".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does the note to the 1910.146(b) definition of inerting say about the atmosphere that inerting produces?

options.A: It makes the space safe to enter without respiratory protection
options.B: It produces an oxygen-enriched atmosphere
options.C: It produces an atmosphere that needs no further testing
options.D: It produces an IDLH oxygen-deficient atmosphere

questions.explanation: Inerting means displacing the atmosphere "by a noncombustible gas (such as nitrogen) to such an extent that the resulting atmosphere is noncombustible," and the note states "This procedure produces an IDLH oxygen-deficient atmosphere."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the note to the 1910.146(b) definition of entry supervisor, may an entry supervisor also serve as an attendant or as an authorized entrant?

options.A: Yes, as long as that person is trained and equipped as required by the section for each role he or she fills
options.B: No, the roles must always be held by different people
options.C: Only in permit spaces with no atmospheric hazard
options.D: Only with written approval from OSHA

questions.explanation: The note says "An entry supervisor also may serve as an attendant or as an authorized entrant, as long as that person is trained and equipped as required by this section for each role he or she fills."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For an air contaminant for which OSHA has not determined a dose or permissible exposure limit, what does the note to the 1910.146(b) definition of hazardous atmosphere say can provide guidance in establishing acceptable atmospheric conditions?

options.A: Only the entrants' own judgment of odor
options.B: Nothing, because such a contaminant can never create a hazardous atmosphere
options.C: Other sources of information, such as Material Safety Data Sheets that comply with the Hazard Communication Standard (1910.1200), published information, and internal documents
options.D: Only a written ruling from the OSHA area office

questions.explanation: The note says "For air contaminants for which OSHA has not determined a dose or permissible exposure limit, other sources of information, such as Material Safety Data Sheets that comply with the Hazard Communication Standard, § 1910.1200 of this part, published information, and internal documents can provide guidance in establishing acceptable atmospheric conditions."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: The note to the 1910.146(b) definition of IDLH names hydrogen fluoride gas and cadmium vapor as materials whose transient effects may be followed by sudden, possibly fatal collapse. How long after exposure?

options.A: 1-2 hours
options.B: 12-72 hours
options.C: 1-2 weeks
options.D: 30 days

questions.explanation: The note says such materials "may produce immediate transient effects that, even if severe, may pass without medical attention, but are followed by sudden, possibly fatal collapse 12-72 hours after exposure."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How does 1910.146(b) define blanking or blinding?

options.A: The absolute closure of a pipe, line, or duct by fastening a solid plate that completely covers the bore and can withstand the maximum pressure with no leakage beyond the plate
options.B: Closing a single valve in the line and tagging it
options.C: Covering the entrance portal of the space with a tarp
options.D: Turning off the lighting inside the space

questions.explanation: Blanking or blinding "means the absolute closure of a pipe, line, or duct by the fastening of a solid plate (such as a spectacle blind or a skillet blind) that completely covers the bore and that is capable of withstanding the maximum pressure of the pipe, line, or duct with no leakage beyond the plate."

questions.topic: Workplace evaluation, warning signs and contractors
questions.question: If the employer decides that its employees will enter permit spaces, what does 1910.146(c)(4) require?

options.A: An oral program explained to each entrant, with nothing in writing
options.B: A program kept confidential from employees
options.C: A program filed with OSHA before the first entry
options.D: A written permit space program that complies with the section and is available for inspection by employees and their authorized representatives

questions.explanation: The employer "shall develop and implement a written permit space program that complies with this section. The written program shall be available for inspection by employees and their authorized representatives."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Workplace evaluation, warning signs and contractors
questions.question: What does 1910.146(c)(3) require of an employer that decides its employees will not enter permit spaces?

options.A: Nothing further, because the section no longer applies to it
options.B: Only a written notice to OSHA that no entries will take place
options.C: Effective measures to prevent its employees from entering the permit spaces
options.D: Entry permits for each permit space every day

questions.explanation: That employer "shall take effective measures to prevent its employees from entering the permit spaces" and must still comply with paragraphs (c)(1), (c)(2), (c)(6) and (c)(8).

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: To use the alternate procedures in 1910.146(c)(5), the employer must be able to demonstrate that the only hazard posed by the permit space is which one?

options.A: A material that could engulf an entrant
options.B: An actual or potential hazardous atmosphere
options.C: Inwardly converging walls
options.D: Moving machinery inside the space

questions.explanation: The employer must demonstrate "that the only hazard posed by the permit space is an actual or potential hazardous atmosphere".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the alternate procedures in 1910.146(c)(5)(ii)(E), where must the air for the continuous forced air ventilation come from?

options.A: From a clean source, and it may not increase the hazards in the space
options.B: From inside the space, recirculated through the fan
options.C: From a compressed oxygen cylinder
options.D: From any source, as long as the fan runs continuously

questions.explanation: The rule says "The air supply for the forced air ventilation shall be from a clean source and may not increase the hazards in the space."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.146(d)(4), on what cost basis must the employer provide equipment such as testing, ventilating, lighting and rescue equipment?

options.A: Employees pay for half of the cost
options.B: Employees pay for their own personal protective equipment only
options.C: Employees pay unless the equipment is reused
options.D: At no cost to employees

questions.explanation: The employer must provide the listed equipment "at no cost to employees, maintain that equipment properly, and ensure that employees use that equipment properly".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does the note to 1910.146(c)(7) say about controlling atmospheric hazards through forced air ventilation?

options.A: It counts as elimination once it has run for one hour
options.B: It counts as elimination when the entry supervisor certifies it
options.C: It does not constitute elimination of the hazards
options.D: It allows reclassification for the rest of the shift

questions.explanation: The note states: "Control of atmospheric hazards through forced air ventilation does not constitute elimination of the hazards."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.146(c)(7)(iv), what must each employee do if hazards arise within a permit space that has been declassified to a non-permit space?

options.A: Exit the space
options.B: Finish the current task and then report the hazard
options.C: Put on a respirator and continue working
options.D: Keep working while the attendant tests the atmosphere

questions.explanation: If hazards arise in a declassified space, "each employee in the space shall exit the space", and the employer then reevaluates it.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Workplace evaluation, warning signs and contractors
questions.question: When does 1910.146(c)(8)(v) require the host employer to debrief the contractor?

options.A: Only if someone is injured during entry
options.B: At the conclusion of the entry operations
options.C: Once a year at the program review
options.D: Before the contractor is hired

questions.explanation: The host employer must "Debrief the contractor at the conclusion of the entry operations" on the program followed and any hazards confronted or created.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How does 1910.146(e)(3) require the completed entry permit to be made available to authorized entrants at the time of entry?

options.A: By mailing it to each entrant's home
options.B: By keeping it locked in the supervisor's office
options.C: By reading it aloud once at the start of each year
options.D: By posting it at the entry portal or by any other equally effective means

questions.explanation: The completed permit "shall be made available at the time of entry to all authorized entrants or their authorized representatives, by posting it at the entry portal or by any other equally effective means, so that the entrants can confirm that pre-entry preparations have been completed."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.146(e)(6), what must be noted on the pertinent entry permit so that appropriate revisions to the permit space program can be made?

options.A: The weather on the day of entry
options.B: Each authorized entrant's home address
options.C: Any problems encountered during an entry operation
options.D: The cost of the entry operation

questions.explanation: Canceled permits are kept at least 1 year for the program review, and "Any problems encountered during an entry operation shall be noted on the pertinent permit so that appropriate revisions to the permit space program can be made."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.146(e)(5), which event requires the entry supervisor to terminate entry and cancel the entry permit?

options.A: A condition that is not allowed under the entry permit arises in or near the permit space
options.B: An authorized entrant takes a scheduled break
options.C: A new attendant takes over at a shift change
options.D: The permit is posted at the entry portal

questions.explanation: The entry supervisor must terminate entry and cancel the permit when entry operations are completed or when "A condition that is not allowed under the entry permit arises in or near the permit space."

questions.topic: Training and duties of entry roles
questions.question: What must the training certification required by 1910.146(g)(4) contain?

options.A: Only the name of the training company
options.B: The trainer's license number and the course price
options.C: The employee's home address and date of birth
options.D: Each employee's name, the signatures or initials of the trainers, and the dates of training

questions.explanation: "The certification shall contain each employee's name, the signatures or initials of the trainers, and the dates of training."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Training and duties of entry roles
questions.question: Under 1910.146(i)(8), what must an attendant do when unauthorized persons approach a permit space while entry is underway?

options.A: Enter the space to warn the entrants in person
options.B: Warn the unauthorized persons that they must stay away from the permit space
options.C: Ignore them unless they enter the space
options.D: Leave the post to call the local OSHA office

questions.explanation: When unauthorized persons approach or enter, the attendant must "Warn the unauthorized persons that they must stay away from the permit space," advise them to exit immediately if they have entered, and inform the authorized entrants and the entry supervisor if they have entered.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.146, Permit-required confined spaces (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Rescue, emergency services and employee participation
questions.question: Under 1910.146(k)(1)(v), what must an employer that designates a rescue team or service provide to it?

options.A: A copy of each entrant's medical records
options.B: Payment in advance for a full year of service
options.C: Access to all permit spaces from which rescue may be necessary, so it can develop appropriate rescue plans and practice rescue operations
options.D: A key to the employer's main office, with nothing else

questions.explanation: The employer shall "Provide the rescue team or service selected with access to all permit spaces from which rescue may be necessary so that the rescue service can develop appropriate rescue plans and practice rescue operations."
